sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- set_session_label: Label the current session with a short 2-5 word description
- google_search: Real-time Google Search grounding via Antigravity
- read_url_content: Read a public web page as markdown via the Antigravity crawler
- generate_image: Generate images via Antigravity OAuth (Gemini image models)
- codemode: Run JavaScript that calls other tools

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- RULES FOR set_session_label (STRICT — NO EXCEPTIONS):
1. ONLY call set_session_label on your VERY FIRST response in a session that has NO label yet.
2. If the session ALREADY HAS a label (from /title, /name, a previous call, or a resumed session), do NOT call set_session_label. The tool will reject it anyway.
3. NEVER rename a session. If the user changes topic mid-session, the original name stays.
4. The ONLY exception: the user explicitly says 'rename this session' or 'change the session name'. In that case, pass force: true.
5. Do NOT ask the user what to name it — just pick a good 2-5 word name from context.
Examples: 'shipping 3DS refactor', 'fix flaky pagination test', 'breadth resolver migration'.
- Use google_search when you need real-time, up-to-date web information, latest news, documentation, or fact checking.
- Pass specific URLs into the urls array if you want the search engine to fetch and analyze specific pages.
- Set instruction to provide special research directives from the lead agent (e.g. focus on issues, compare benchmarks, restrict time range).
- Use read_url_content when you have a specific URL whose contents you need, instead of guessing from a search result summary.
- One URL per call, and prefer the page that holds the answer over a site root or a category index.
- Long pages return their beginning and save the full page to a local file; read or search that file instead of fetching the URL again.
- It cannot log in, run JavaScript, or read local and private addresses, so do not use it for those.
- Use generate_image when the user asks to create, draw, or generate an image.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description:
Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

Codemode: `tools.read(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description:
Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

Codemode: `tools.bash(args)` resolves to a string.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Codemode: `tools.edit(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description:
Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

Codemode: `tools.write(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: set_session_label
toolsAdded.description:
Set a short label for the current session. The label is shown in the terminal title, a persistent banner, and the session list. Keep it to 2-5 words. IMPORTANT: This tool will REJECT the call if the session already has a label, unless force is set to true. Only use force when the user explicitly asks to rename.

Codemode: `tools.set_session_label(args)` resolves to a string.

label.description: Short 2-5 word session label, e.g. 'fix checkout tax bug'

force.description: Force-rename even if the session already has a label. Only set to true when the user explicitly asks to rename the session.

toolsAdded.name: google_search
toolsAdded.description:
Search the web using Google Search via Antigravity Grounding. Returns a compact evidence brief with source citations. Use this whenever current, real-time information or web research is needed.

Codemode: `tools.google_search(args)` resolves to a string.

instruction.description: Specific directive or focus from the lead agent (e.g., '重点关注英文社区近七天的讨论', 'focus on GitHub issues and benchmarks', 'ignore marketing announcements').

urls.description: Optional specific URLs to fetch and analyze alongside the search.

thinking.description: Enable deeper thinking for complex analysis (default: false).

toolsAdded.name: read_url_content
toolsAdded.description:
Read a public web page through Google's Antigravity crawler and return it as markdown. Use it for documentation, articles, changelogs, and standards pages when search snippets are not enough. The crawl runs on Google's side: no JavaScript execution, no cookies, and no pages behind a login — for those, ask the user to open the page in their browser.

Codemode: `tools.read_url_content(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: generate_image
toolsAdded.description:
Generate an image via Antigravity using the signed-in Google account, optionally guided by local reference images. Saves under .pi/generated-images/ unless path is set.

Codemode: `tools.generate_image(args)` resolves to a string.

items.description: Project-relative reference image path (PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF).

referenceImages.description: Reference images to send alongside the prompt.

path.description: Project-relative file or directory to save the image.

toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.
- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /home/lucid/.nvm/versions/node/v22.22.2/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/codemode.md first.

Keep a trail's description current with `entire trail update`. When referencing a trail or change, include its full URL. Post feedback on a trail as findings (`entire trail finding`), never as trail comments; comments are for people. Commits capture the AI session as a checkpoint automatically; only create checkpoints manually when the user asks. If a setup or destructive command (enable, disable, clean, auth) is needed, always ask the user before running it.

- [@vitejs/plugin-react](https://github.com/vitejs/vite-plugin-react/blob/main/packages/plugin-react) uses [Oxc](https://oxc.rs)
- [@vitejs/plugin-react-swc](https://github.com/vitejs/vite-plugin-react/blob/main/packages/plugin-react-swc) uses [SWC](https://swc.rs/)

## React Compiler

The React Compiler is not enabled on this template because of its impact on dev & build performances. To add it, see [this documentation](https://react.dev/learn/react-compiler/installation).

## Expanding the Oxlint configuration

If you are developing a production application, we recommend enabling type-aware lint rules by installing `oxlint-tsgolint` and editing `.oxlintrc.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "./node_modules/oxlint/configuration_schema.json",
  "plugins": ["react", "typescript", "oxc"],
  "options": {
    "typeAware": true
  },
  "rules": {
    "react/rules-of-hooks": "error",
    "react/only-export-components": ["warn", { "allowConstantExport": true }]
  }
}
```

See the [Oxlint rules documentation](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules) for the full list of rules and categories.

Yes—the eye works better than another status badge. I made **VEGA** larger, scaled the eye to match, and kept the glass pill for the three passive states:

- **Anomaly detected:** green, open eye.

import type { Point } from './topologyLayout'

const DOT_STEP = 36
const HOVER_RADIUS = 128

export function drawTopologyDots(
  ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D,
  width: number,
  height: number,
  origin: Point,
  zoom: number,
  hover: Point & { strength: number },
) {
  const step = DOT_STEP * zoom
  const firstX = (origin.x % step) - step
  const firstY = (origin.y % step) - step
  const base = new Path2D()
  const soft = new Path2D()
  const bright = new Path2D()
  const reacting = hover.strength > 0.01

  for (let y = firstY; y <= height + step; y += step) {
    for (let x = firstX; x <= width + step; x += step) {
      const dx = x - hover.x
      const dy = y - hover.y
      let influence = 0
      if (reacting && Math.abs(dx) < HOVER_RADIUS && Math.abs(dy) < HOVER_RADIUS) {
        influence = hover.strength * Math.max(0, 1 - Math.hypot(dx, dy) / HOVER_RADIUS) ** 2
      }
      // Nudge the dots away from the pointer while brightening the nearest ones.
      const px = x + dx * influence * 0.24
      const py = y + dy * influence * 0.24
      const radius = 0.85 + influence * 1.1
      const path = influence > 0.38 ? bright : influence > 0.07 ? soft : base
      path.moveTo(px + radius, py)
      path.arc(px, py, radius, 0, Math.PI * 2)
    }
  }

  ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(139, 174, 205, 0.15)'
  ctx.fill(base)
  if (!reacting) return
  ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(125, 190, 227, 0.27)'
  ctx.fill(soft)
  ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(153, 222, 255, 0.5)'
  ctx.fill(bright)
}

  path.quadraticCurveTo(x + shoulder, y + shoulder, x, y + size)
  path.quadraticCurveTo(x - shoulder, y + shoulder, x - size, y)
  path.quadraticCurveTo(x - shoulder, y - shoulder, x, y - size)

}

export function drawTopologyDots(
  ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D,
  width: number,
  height: number,
  origin: Point,
  zoom: number,
  hover: TopologyHover,
) {
  const step = DOT_STEP * zoom
  const firstX = (origin.x % step) - step
  const firstY = (origin.y % step) - step
  const base = new Path2D()
  const radius = 106 + 48 * hover.motion
  const reacting = hover.strength > 0.01

  for (let y = firstY; y <= height + step; y += step) {
    for (let x = firstX; x <= width + step; x += step) {
      const dx = x - hover.x
      const dy = y - hover.y
      const distance = reacting && Math.abs(dx) < radius && Math.abs(dy) < radius
        ? Math.hypot(dx, dy)
        : radius
      if (distance >= radius) {
        addStar(base, x, y, BASE_SIZE)
        continue
      }

      // Like the portfolio footer, nearby stars scale up and push radially away.
      const influence = hover.strength * (1 - distance / radius) ** 1.5
      const push = (22 + 8 * hover.motion) * influence / Math.max(14, distance)
      const size = BASE_SIZE + (4.3 + hover.motion) * influence
      const clearCenter = 1 - hover.strength * Math.max(0, 1 - distance / 18)
      const opacity = (0.15 + 0.7 * influence) * clearCenter
      // Keep distant stars low contrast; only the center of the field turns white.
      ctx.fillStyle = `rgba(${Math.round(139 + 116 * influence)}, ${Math.round(174 + 81 * influence)}, ${Math.round(205 + 50 * influence)}, ${opacity})`
      ctx.beginPath()
      addStar(ctx, x + dx * push, y + dy * push, size)
      ctx.fill()
    }
  }

  ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(139, 174, 205, 0.15)'
  ctx.fill(base)
}

import { create } from 'zustand'
import type {
  CouncilSignal,
  MonitoredNode,
  NetworkEdge,
  NodeStatus,
  ObserverQA,
  OracleAssessment,
  ScenarioId,
  ScoutFinding,
  StoredEvent,
  ThreatMode,
  VegaStage,
  WardenAuditEntry,
  WardenDecision,
  Window,
} from '../contracts/vega'
import { SCENARIOS } from '../data/scenarios'

export interface ObserverMessage {
  id: string
  role: 'user' | 'vega'
  text: string
  qa?: ObserverQA
  timestamp: string
}

export interface BackendStateSnapshot {
  threat_mode: ThreatMode
  active_window_id: string
  ttl_seconds_remaining: number
  nodes: MonitoredNode[]
  edges: NetworkEdge[]
  windows: Window[]
  events: StoredEvent[]
  findings: ScoutFinding[]
  council_signal: CouncilSignal | null
  oracle_assessment: OracleAssessment | null
  warden_decision: WardenDecision | null
}

export type LiveConnectionStatus = 'disconnected' | 'connecting' | 'connected'

interface VegaState {
  dataMode: 'SIMULATED' | 'LIVE'
  liveStatus: LiveConnectionStatus
  scenarioId: ScenarioId
  stage: VegaStage
  threatMode: ThreatMode
  isPlaying: boolean
  playbackSpeed: number
  elapsedMs: number
  ttlSecondsRemaining: number

  nodes: MonitoredNode[]
  edges: NetworkEdge[]
  windows: Window[]
  activeWindowId: string
  events: StoredEvent[]
  findings: ScoutFinding[]
  councilSignal: CouncilSignal | null
  oracleAssessment: OracleAssessment | null
  wardenDecision: WardenDecision | null

  selectedNodeId: string | null
  selectedEventId: string | null
  chronosExpanded: boolean
  chronosCursorIndex: number | null
  observerOpen: boolean
  observerMessages: ObserverMessage[]
  presenterOpen: boolean

  // Actions
  setDataMode: (mode: 'SIMULATED' | 'LIVE') => void
  setLiveStatus: (status: LiveConnectionStatus) => void
  resetLiveBaseline: () => void
  hydrateSnapshot: (snapshot: BackendStateSnapshot) => void
  loadScenario: (scenarioId: ScenarioId) => void
  setStage: (stage: VegaStage) => void
  setThreatMode: (mode: ThreatMode) => void
  setPlaying: (playing: boolean) => void
  setPlaybackSpeed: (speed: number) => void
  setElapsedMs: (ms: number) => void
  tickTtl: (deltaSec: number) => void
  pushEvent: (event: StoredEvent) => void
  pushFinding: (finding: ScoutFinding) => void
  markEventsSuspicious: (eventIds: string[]) => void
  upsertWindow: (window: Window) => void
  setCouncilSignal: (signal: CouncilSignal | null) => void
  setOracleAssessment: (assessment: OracleAssessment | null) => void
  setWardenDecision: (decision: WardenDecision | null) => void
  updateNodeStatus: (sourceId: string, status: NodeStatus) => void
  markEdgeAnomalous: (edgeId: string, anomalous: boolean) => void
  updateWindowStatus: (windowId: string, status: Window['status']) => void
  setActiveWindowId: (windowId: string) => void
  selectNode: (sourceId: string | null) => void
  selectEvent: (eventId: string | null) => void
  setChronosExpanded: (expanded: boolean) => void
  setChronosCursorIndex: (index: number | null) => void
  setObserverOpen: (open: boolean) => void
  addObserverMessage: (msg: ObserverMessage) => void
  setPresenterOpen: (open: boolean) => void
  appendWardenAudit: (entry: WardenAuditEntry) => void
  updateWardenExecution: (
    patch: Partial<Pick<WardenDecision, 'approval_status' | 'approval_ref' | 'execution_status'>>,
  ) => void
}

const initialScenario = SCENARIOS['sev1-exfil']

export const useVegaStore = create<VegaState>((set) => ({
  dataMode: 'SIMULATED',
  liveStatus: 'disconnected',
  scenarioId: initialScenario.id,
  stage: 'panopticon',
  threatMode: 'WATCH',
          pseudonym: 'cluster-hub',
          role: 'VEGA Ingest & Swarm Hub',
          cluster: 'core',
          status: 'healthy',
          heartbeat_age_sec: 0,
          identity_sealed: false,
        },
      ],
      edges: [],
      windows: [],
      activeWindowId: 'W-1000',
      events: [],
      findings: [],
      councilSignal: null,
      oracleAssessment: null,
      wardenDecision: null,
      selectedNodeId: null,
      selectedEventId: null,
      chronosCursorIndex: null,
      observerMessages: [],
    }),

  hydrateSnapshot: (snapshot) =>
    set((state) => {
      const flaggedIds = new Set<string>()
      for (const f of snapshot.findings) {
        for (const eid of f.evidence_event_ids) flaggedIds.add(eid)
      }
      if (snapshot.council_signal) {
        for (const eid of snapshot.council_signal.evidence_event_ids) flaggedIds.add(eid)
      }
      const events = snapshot.events.map((ev) =>
        flaggedIds.has(ev.event_id) ? { ...ev, suspicious: true } : ev,
      )
      return {
        threatMode: snapshot.threat_mode,
        activeWindowId: snapshot.active_window_id,
        ttlSecondsRemaining: snapshot.ttl_seconds_remaining,
        nodes: snapshot.nodes,
        edges: snapshot.edges,
        windows: snapshot.windows,
        events,
        findings: snapshot.findings,
        councilSignal: snapshot.council_signal,
        oracleAssessment: snapshot.oracle_assessment,
        wardenDecision: snapshot.warden_decision,
        selectedNodeId:
          state.selectedNodeId && snapshot.nodes.some((n) => n.source_id === state.selectedNodeId)
            ? state.selectedNodeId
            : null,
      }
    }),

  loadScenario: (scenarioId) => {
    const sc = SCENARIOS[scenarioId]
    set({
      scenarioId,
      stage: 'panopticon',
      threatMode: 'WATCH',
      isPlaying: true,
      elapsedMs: 0,
      ttlSecondsRemaining: sc.retention_seconds,

import type { ScenarioId, VegaStage } from '../contracts/vega'
import { useVegaStore } from '../store/useVegaStore'
import type { VegaDataSource } from './dataSource'
import { LiveStreamSource } from './liveSource'
import { mockSource } from './mockSource'

const liveSource = new LiveStreamSource()

function activeSource(): VegaDataSource {
  return useVegaStore.getState().dataMode === 'LIVE' ? liveSource : mockSource
}

export function switchDataMode(mode: 'SIMULATED' | 'LIVE', force = false) {
  const current = useVegaStore.getState().dataMode
  if (current === mode && !force) return
  activeSource().stop()
  useVegaStore.getState().setDataMode(mode)
  activeSource().start()
}

export async function flushLiveWindow() {
  if (useVegaStore.getState().dataMode === 'LIVE') {
    await liveSource.flushWindow()
  }
}

Description:
Redesign the VEGA frontend dashboard and topology while keeping the existing monitoring, Council, and Warden flows intact.

- Replace the status header with a floating glass VEGA wordmark and put the animated, state-colored eye inside the circular VEGA-CORE hub.
- Make the topology pannable, with a sparse hover-reactive dotted background and draggable VM cards that keep their connections and do not overlap.
- Keep anomaly injection on the topology; open node details only through an explicit inspection action.
- Add canvas zoom from 50% to 100% with on-screen and keyboard controls, preserving wheel panning, node dragging, and the chosen zoom after inspection.

summary:
## Goal
Continue the minimalist VEGA dashboard redesign in `frontend/`, keeping the topology interactive and the monitoring, Council, and Warden states clear without restoring the old status header. The latest request was to let users zoom out.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Keep the centered VEGA wordmark floating over the graph with a soft, borderless glass halo. The user dropped the separate font redesign request.
- Keep background dots sparse, faint, and hollow. They should react to hover, not compete with the graph or interfere with dragging.
- Keep VM cards draggable and non-overlapping. Clicking a card inspects it; **Inject Anomaly** must not open it automatically.
- Keep frontend commits separate from unrelated, uncommitted `backend/` changes.
- Use the separate [frontend redesign trail](https://entire.com/gh/lllucidll/-/trails/2), not Oracle Council. For Entire commands, read `entire agent-help` and the exact subcommand help, keep the description current with `entire trail update`, use full URLs, and post feedback as findings rather than comments. Ask before setup/destructive commands; commits capture checkpoints automatically.

## Progress
### Done
- [x] Replaced `TopHud.tsx` with the floating `VegaBrand.tsx` wordmark. Moved the animated eye into the 160 px circular VEGA-CORE hub, replacing its checkmark.
- [x] Preserved eye states: green closed while monitoring; green open and scanning on anomaly; `#7851a9` purple and scanning during Council investigation; red serpent slit during Warden takeover. Core fill, border, and glow match the passive eye colors. Eyelid opening takes 500 ms; reduced-motion preferences are respected. Warden still shows **VEGA HAS ASSUMED CONTROL** and explicit authorization status.
- [x] Added wheel and blank-space drag panning, hover-reactive hollow dots, and draggable VM cards. Connections and particles follow the cards, nearby cards make room, and the hub stays fixed in world coordinates. Clicking VEGA recenters.
- [x] Updated `frontend/src/engine/mockSource.ts` and `frontend/src/engine/liveSource.ts` so injection highlights the affected VM without opening it. `PresenterBar.tsx` offers **Next: Inspect Node** after a finding.
- [x] Pushed the redesign baseline to [`frontend-redesign`](https://github.com/llLucidll/VEGA/tree/frontend-redesign) in `fa967dc` (`Redesign the VEGA dashboard and topology`). Linked it to the [Entire change](https://entire.com/gh/lllucidll/-/trails/2/changes/VEGA/2).
- [x] Implemented local zoom from 50% to 100% in 10% steps. Bottom-right **− / +** controls change zoom; clicking the percentage resets it. With canvas focus, `-`, `+`/`=`, and `0` do the same. Wheel still pans. Lint, production build, Chrome zoom checks, and graph regression checks passed. Updated the trail description.

### In Progress
- [ ] Zoom changes are implemented and verified but not committed or pushed. The local frontend diff is limited to `frontend/src/components/stages/PanopticonCanvas.tsx` and `frontend/src/engine/topologyLayout.ts`.

### Blocked
- None.

## Key Decisions
- **Reuse the topology camera**: `setCanvasZoom` adjusts the existing camera. Cards and positions scale together below 100% to prevent overlap. Inspection keeps its existing zoom-in behavior, and exiting restores the chosen topology zoom.
- **Separate gestures**: Wheel and blank-space drag pan; a VM drag moves the card and suppresses click-on-drop; zoom has separate controls.
- **Use measured collision bounds**: `packTopology` uses unscaled card dimensions, keeps the hub anchored, and places the dragged card before its neighbors.
- **Share status state**: `useVegaEyeState` drives the core, Council, and Warden visuals. `--vega-oracle` in `frontend/src/index.css` is the source of the exact Council purple.

## Next Steps
1. If asked to publish the zoom changes, stage only the two frontend files, commit, and push to `frontend-redesign`. Leave backend changes untouched.
2. Keep the [frontend redesign trail](https://entire.com/gh/lllucidll/-/trails/2) current as the scope changes.

## Critical Context
- Repo: `gh/llLucidll/VEGA`. Current branch: `frontend-redesign`, tracking `origin/frontend-redesign`; the last verified remote commit is `fa967dc05666da26ea491b5a2afb5e7a2f30f585`.
- Main UI code: `frontend/src/components/stages/PanopticonCanvas.tsx`, `frontend/src/components/layout/VegaBrand.tsx`, `frontend/src/components/layout/VegaEye.tsx`, `frontend/src/store/useVegaEyeState.ts`, `frontend/src/engine/drawTopologyDots.ts`, and `frontend/src/engine/topologyLayout.ts`.
- The dot motion was inspired by the [PortfolioWebsite footer source](https://github.com/llLucidll/PortfolioWebsite/blob/master/self.js), but the final markers are hollow circles, not stars.
- Chrome checks used simulated mode. Zoom tests confirmed limits, keyboard and click reset, wheel panning, node dragging without overlaps, and zoom retention after inspection. Preview: `/tmp/vega-topology-zoomed-out.png`.

---

**Turn Context (split turn):**

## Original Request
Add a floating “liquid glass halo” telemetry panel in the dashboard’s top-right corner, without bringing back the removed header. Show event ingestion rate, TTL, the other metric removed with the header, and active nodes online. Suggest other useful metrics.

## Progress So Far
- Inspected the removed `TopHud.tsx` at commit `dce31c9`. It read `threatMode`, `activeWindowId`, `ttlSecondsRemaining`, `councilSignal`, `dataMode`, and `liveStatus`; TTL was formatted as `MM:SS`. The user did not specify which other removed metric to restore.
- Inspected the dashboard layout, styles, Zustand store, live and simulated sources, and backend telemetry fields. No edits, tests, or final metric choices are shown.
- Confirmed that simulated mode ticks TTL once per second while playing. Its ambient particles are spawned separately from event ingestion. Backend retention defaults to 600 seconds, and backend state initializes TTL from that setting.

## Context Needed to Continue
- Current branch is `frontend-redesign`, at redesign commit `fa967dc`. The working tree already contains modified and untracked files, including backend changes and frontend edits to `PanopticonCanvas.tsx` and `topologyLayout.ts`.
- `BackendStateSnapshot` exposes `active_window_id`, `ttl_seconds_remaining`, `nodes`, `edges`, `windows`, `events`, `findings`, and council/oracle/warden outputs. The backend node model exposes `heartbeat_age_sec`; the inspected state code resets it to zero on a heartbeat. No online-node rule or ingestion-rate calculation was selected.

sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- RULES FOR set_session_label (STRICT — NO EXCEPTIONS):
1. ONLY call set_session_label on your VERY FIRST response in a session that has NO label yet.
2. If the session ALREADY HAS a label (from /title, /name, a previous call, or a resumed session), do NOT call set_session_label. The tool will reject it anyway.
3. NEVER rename a session. If the user changes topic mid-session, the original name stays.
4. The ONLY exception: the user explicitly says 'rename this session' or 'change the session name'. In that case, pass force: true.
5. Do NOT ask the user what to name it — just pick a good 2-5 word name from context.
Examples: 'shipping 3DS refactor', 'fix flaky pagination test', 'breadth resolver migration'.
- Use google_search when you need real-time, up-to-date web information, latest news, documentation, or fact checking.
- Pass specific URLs into the urls array if you want the search engine to fetch and analyze specific pages.
- Set instruction to provide special research directives from the lead agent (e.g. focus on issues, compare benchmarks, restrict time range).
- Use read_url_content when you have a specific URL whose contents you need, instead of guessing from a search result summary.
- One URL per call, and prefer the page that holds the answer over a site root or a category index.
- Long pages return their beginning and save the full page to a local file; read or search that file instead of fetching the URL again.
- It cannot log in, run JavaScript, or read local and private addresses, so do not use it for those.
- Use generate_image when the user asks to create, draw, or generate an image.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.description:
Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

Codemode: `tools.read(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description:
Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

Codemode: `tools.bash(args)` resolves to a string.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Codemode: `tools.edit(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

content.text:
`stash@{0}` (`4584cc5`) contains **rolling Oracle Council case support** from `warden-scaffold`. It changes 10 files:

- **Cross-window context:** Oracle combines recent SEV1 handoffs into one case, looking back 15 minutes by default and using only evidence cited by those handoffs.
- **Per-host verdicts:** Oracle reviews each host separately and reuses successful verdicts when the evidence hasn’t changed. It can flag a shared destination without assuming a common actor or recommending fleet-wide containment.
- **Reset and concurrency:** Superseded reviews can’t publish stale results, and a demo reset clears the review cache.
- **UI and tests:** `frontend/src/components/stages/CouncilView.tsx` shows which Sentinel windows the case covers. `backend/tests/test_oracle_bridge.py` adds coverage for cross-window reviews, cache reuse, and reset behavior.

The stash is still intact and hasn’t been applied to `main`.

## Goal
Continue the minimalist VEGA frontend redesign: keep the topology interactive, telemetry readable, and the monitoring, Council, and Warden states clear. The redesign is published; the most recent request was to identify what remained uncommitted on `frontend-redesign`.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Keep the centered VEGA wordmark, soft glass halo, and recenter action. The separate font redesign was dropped. The user later requested a semi-translucent full-width header for visual separation, but no separate telemetry glass pill.
- Put telemetry in a news-style strip beneath the header. It should move right to left and remain visible when inspecting a node.
- Keep background dots sparse, faint, hollow, and hover-reactive. Use concentric circles centered on VEGA-CORE rather than a square grid.
- Keep VM cards draggable and non-overlapping. Clicking a card inspects it; **Inject Anomaly** must not open it automatically.
- Keep frontend redesign commits separate from unrelated live-mode, VEGA-CORE artwork, and `backend/` changes. Do not discard or publish those changes without direction.
- Use the [frontend redesign trail](https://entire.com/gh/lllucidll/-/trails/2), not Oracle Council. Read `entire agent-help` and exact subcommand help, update the description with `entire trail update`, use full URLs, and post feedback as findings rather than comments. Ask before setup or destructive commands; commits capture checkpoints automatically.

## Progress
### Done
- [x] Replaced `TopHud.tsx` with `VegaBrand.tsx` and moved the animated eye into the 160 px circular VEGA-CORE hub. Preserved closed green monitoring, open green scanning on anomaly, exact `#7851a9` Council scanning, and red serpent-slit Warden takeover. Core fill, border, and glow match the eye; opening takes 500 ms and respects reduced motion. Warden still displays **VEGA HAS ASSUMED CONTROL** and explicit authorization status.
- [x] Added wheel and blank-space drag panning, draggable cards, collision avoidance, and a fixed world-space hub. Connections and particles follow cards. Clicking VEGA recenters. Baseline changes to `mockSource.ts`, `liveSource.ts`, and `PresenterBar.tsx` kept anomaly injection separate from inspection and added **Next: Inspect Node**.
- [x] Added 50–100% zoom in 10% steps with bottom-right **− / +**, percentage reset, and focused-canvas `-`, `+`/`=`, `0` shortcuts. Inspection retains its zoom-in effect and restores the chosen topology zoom afterward.
- [x] Iterated from a floating liquid-glass telemetry panel to a borderless readout, then to a semi-translucent full-width header with a thin divider. `DashboardHeader.tsx` centers the wordmark and now mounts `TelemetryTicker.tsx` beneath the header, with no separate pill.
- [x] The ticker shows ingest rate, retention TTL, active window ID, nodes online, captured/flagged counts, snapshot preservation, and source status. It loops right to left, pauses on hover or button without stopping data updates, and becomes a static wrapping row with reduced motion. Reduced transparency uses an opaque fallback. Suggested p95 ingestion lag as a future metric; not implemented.
- [x] Kept the same ticker mounted across `panopticon` and `ghost_protocol`, preserving scroll position and pause state while the node drawer opens or closes. The drawer clears the ticker even when the reduced-motion layout wraps on mobile. The ticker stays hidden in Council and Warden views.
- [x] Added `spaceTopology` in `frontend/src/engine/topologyLayout.ts`: endpoints form an equally spaced ring around VEGA-CORE, and the radius grows to clear measured card bounds. Roster changes rebalance the ring after any active drag; events from known endpoints do not reset manual placement. Removed unused `d3-force` dependencies and added `frontend/tests/topologyLayout.test.mjs`.
- [x] Replaced the square grid and old dashed orbit overlay with wider-spaced, hollow concentric dots. `drawTopologyDots` keeps the rings centered on the hub through zoom, pan, and recenter, with the existing cursor reaction. Browser and geometry checks passed.
- [x] Published the baseline in [`fa967dc`](https://github.com/llLucidll/VEGA/commit/fa967dc05666da26ea491b5a2afb5e7a2f30f585), the header/ticker/zoom/orbit work in [`4ddb48d`](https://github.com/llLucidll/VEGA/commit/4ddb48d4176a89c8f500cccc9c8844778ca2a5c2), and only the two concentric-dot changes in [`db5a908`](https://github.com/llLucidll/VEGA/commit/db5a90887624fc7d7b53a10fa75b61133993858f). Tested the exact staged frontend before both later pushes: lint, production build, layout tests, and Chrome smoke checks passed. Updated the redesign trail.
- [x] Audited the remaining local changes without modifying anything. Local `HEAD` and `origin/frontend-redesign` both point to `db5a908`; nothing is staged and there are no unpushed commits.

### In Progress
- [ ] No redesign work is pending. The working tree still holds unrelated frontend live-mode changes and VEGA-CORE artwork (9 modified frontend files and 3 untracked PNGs), plus 16 modified and 16 untracked backend files. These were intentionally excluded from the redesign pushes.

### Blocked
- None.

## Key Decisions
- **Reuse the topology camera**: `setCanvasZoom` scales cards and positions together; wheel and blank-space drag pan, while node drag suppresses click-on-drop. Clicking the wordmark uses `PanopticonHandle.recenter`.
- **Separate automatic spacing from manual placement**: `spaceTopology` uses sorted endpoint IDs, equal angular slots, and measured rectangular bounds. `packTopology` anchors the hub and prioritizes the dragged card. Manual placement survives until the roster changes; growing rings may require pan or zoom.
- **Share status state**: `useVegaEyeState` drives core, Council, and Warden visuals; `--vega-oracle` in `frontend/src/index.css` provides the Council purple.
- **Preserve ticker identity and clearance**: `DashboardHeader` measures its stack with `ResizeObserver`, passes the height through `App.tsx`, and `GhostProtocolPanel` uses it to avoid overlapping the ticker.
- **Use mode-aware telemetry**: `sampleTelemetry`, `measureTelemetry`, and `formatTtl` live in `frontend/src/engine/telemetryMetrics.ts`. Rate is a 60-second window ending at latest replay ingest or current live time. Simulated online counts use recent heartbeats; live counts use telemetry in the last 120 seconds. sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- RULES FOR set_session_label (STRICT — NO EXCEPTIONS):
1. ONLY call set_session_label on your VERY FIRST response in a session that has NO label yet.
2. If the session ALREADY HAS a label (from /title, /name, a previous call, or a resumed session), do NOT call set_session_label. The tool will reject it anyway.
3. NEVER rename a session. If the user changes topic mid-session, the original name stays.
4. The ONLY exception: the user explicitly says 'rename this session' or 'change the session name'. In that case, pass force: true.
5. Do NOT ask the user what to name it — just pick a good 2-5 word name from context.
Examples: 'shipping 3DS refactor', 'fix flaky pagination test', 'breadth resolver migration'.
- Use google_search when you need real-time, up-to-date web information, latest news, documentation, or fact checking.
- Pass specific URLs into the urls array if you want the search engine to fetch and analyze specific pages.
- Set instruction to provide special research directives from the lead agent (e.g. focus on issues, compare benchmarks, restrict time range).
- Use read_url_content when you have a specific URL whose contents you need, instead of guessing from a search result summary.
- One URL per call, and prefer the page that holds the answer over a site root or a category index.
- Long pages return their beginning and save the full page to a local file; read or search that file instead of fetching the URL again.
- It cannot log in, run JavaScript, or read local and private addresses, so do not use it for those.
- Use generate_image when the user asks to create, draw, or generate an image.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description:
Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

Codemode: `tools.read(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description:
Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

Codemode: `tools.bash(args)` resolves to a string.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Codemode: `tools.edit(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description:
Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

Codemode: `tools.write(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: set_session_label
toolsAdded.description:
Set a short label for the current session. The label is shown in the terminal title, a persistent banner, and the session list. Keep it to 2-5 words. IMPORTANT: This tool will REJECT the call if the session already has a label, unless force is set to true. Only use force when the user explicitly asks to rename.

Codemode: `tools.set_session_label(args)` resolves to a string.

label.description: Short 2-5 word session label, e.g. 'fix checkout tax bug'

force.description: Force-rename even if the session already has a label. Only set to true when the user explicitly asks to rename the session.

toolsAdded.name: google_search
toolsAdded.description:
Search the web using Google Search via Antigravity Grounding. Returns a compact evidence brief with source citations. Use this whenever current, real-time information or web research is needed.

Codemode: `tools.google_search(args)` resolves to a string.

instruction.description: Specific directive or focus from the lead agent (e.g., '重点关注英文社区近七天的讨论', 'focus on GitHub issues and benchmarks', 'ignore marketing announcements').

urls.description: Optional specific URLs to fetch and analyze alongside the search.

thinking.description: Enable deeper thinking for complex analysis (default: false).

toolsAdded.name: read_url_content
toolsAdded.description:
Read a public web page through Google's Antigravity crawler and return it as markdown. Use it for documentation, articles, changelogs, and standards pages when search snippets are not enough. The crawl runs on Google's side: no JavaScript execution, no cookies, and no pages behind a login — for those, ask the user to open the page in their browser.

Codemode: `tools.read_url_content(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: generate_image
toolsAdded.description:
Generate an image via Antigravity using the signed-in Google account, optionally guided by local reference images. Saves under .pi/generated-images/ unless path is set.

Codemode: `tools.generate_image(args)` resolves to a string.

items.description: Project-relative reference image path (PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF).

referenceImages.description: Reference images to send alongside the prompt.

path.description: Project-relative file or directory to save the image.

toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.
- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /home/lucid/.nvm/versions/node/v22.22.2/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/codemode.md first.

"""Track C: Warden policy-gated containment with TypeSafe AI Jev System One routing."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from collections.abc import Iterable
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from typing import Any, Protocol

from oracle.context import PROTECTED_HOSTS

from ..config import settings
from ..models import (
    CouncilSignal,
    OracleAssessment,
    PolicyCheck,
    ScoutFinding,
    StoredEvent,
    WardenActionType,
    WardenAuditEntry,
    WardenDecision,
)
from .enforcer import ContainmentExecutor, DryRunContainmentExecutor

LOG = logging.getLogger("vega.warden")


def _now_ts() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%H:%M:%S.%f")[:-3] + "Z"


def _audit(actor: str, message: str, status: str = "info") -> WardenAuditEntry:
    return WardenAuditEntry(
        id=f"aud-{int(datetime.now(timezone.utc).timestamp() * 1000)}-{abs(hash(message)) % 10000}",
        timestamp=_now_ts(),
        actor=actor,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        message=message,
        status=status,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    )


@dataclass
class JevEvaluation:
    available: bool
    action_choice: WardenActionType
    confidence: float
    probabilities: dict[str, float]
    credential_compromise: float
    host_compromise: float
    safe_to_automate: float
    model: str
    error: str | None = None

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "available": self.available,
            "action_choice": self.action_choice,
            "confidence": round(self.confidence, 4),
            "probabilities": {k: round(v, 4) for k, v in self.probabilities.items()},
            "credential_compromise": round(self.credential_compromise, 4),
            "host_compromise": round(self.host_compromise, 4),
            "safe_to_automate": round(self.safe_to_automate, 4),
            "model": self.model,
            "error": self.error,

"""Tests for Warden + TypeSafe AI Jev System One routing and live containment executor."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import httpx
import pytest

from oracle import context as oracle_context
from oracle.sentinel_bridge import OracleBridge
from vega.council.enforcer import DryRunContainmentExecutor, LiveContainmentExecutor
from vega.council.warden import JevEvaluation, JevWardenService, TypeSafeJevEvaluator
from vega.models import (
    CouncilSignal,
    DefenderOpinion,
    OracleAssessment,
    ProsecutorOpinion,
    ScoutFinding,
    StewardOpinion,
    StoredEvent,
    VmVerdict,
)
from vega.state import VegaRuntimeState

FIXTURE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "oracle" / "fixtures" / "three_vm_request.json"


def _fixture():
    raw = json.loads(FIXTURE.read_text())
    signal = CouncilSignal.model_validate(raw["signal"])
    findings = [ScoutFinding.model_validate(f) for f in raw["findings"]]
    events = [StoredEvent.model_validate(e) for e in raw["events"]]
    return signal, findings, events


def _assessment(verdicts: list[VmVerdict], signal_id: str = "sig-1") -> OracleAssessment:
    return OracleAssessment(
        incident_id="INC-100",
        signal_id=signal_id,
        assessment="Correlated secret access, archive staging, and unapproved egress.",
        competing_explanations=[],
        cited_policies=[],
        historical_context="No prior incidents.",
        uncertainty="Low",
        recommended_action="Isolate compromised host and revoke credentials.",
        recommended_scope="host:vm-a",
        model_version="gemini-3.5-flash-lite",
        created_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
        verdicts=verdicts,
        council_ms=420,
    )


def _verdict(source_id: str, verdict: str) -> VmVerdict:
    return VmVerdict(
        source_id=source_id,
        verdict=verdict,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        prosecutor=ProsecutorOpinion(score=0.92 if verdict == "CONTAIN" else 0.1, reason="evidence"),
        defender=DefenderOpinion(score=0.1 if verdict == "CONTAIN" else 0.9, hypothesis="benign", reason="check"),
        steward=StewardOpinion(allowed=True, policy_ids=["POL-CONTAIN-01"], reason="allowed"),
    )


class StubJev:
    def __init__(self, result: JevEvaluation) -> None:
        self.result = result
        self.last_state: dict | None = None

    async def evaluate(self, state: dict) -> JevEvaluation:
        self.last_state = state
        return self.result


async def test_jev_high_confidence_auto_contains_without_human():
    signal, findings, events = _fixture()
    assessment = _assessment(
        [_verdict("vm-a", "CONTAIN"), _verdict("vm-b", "NO_ACTION")],
        signal_id=signal.signal_id,
    )
    jev = StubJev(
        JevEvaluation(
            available=True,
            action_choice="quarantine_and_revoke",
            confidence=0.94,
            probabilities={
                "quarantine_and_revoke": 0.95,
                "quarantine_host": 0.04,
                "revoke_credentials": 0.01,
                "escalate_human": 0.0,
            },
            credential_compromise=0.96,
            host_compromise=0.93,
            safe_to_automate=0.91,
            model="jev-1.13.0",
        )
    )
    executor = DryRunContainmentExecutor({"vm-a": "auth0|demo"})
    warden = JevWardenService(jev=jev, executor=executor, vm_subjects={"vm-a": "auth0|demo"})

    decision = await warden.evaluate(assessment, signal=signal, findings=findings, events=events)
    assert decision is not None
    assert decision.requires_human_approval is False
    assert decision.approval_status == "approved"
    assert decision.approval_ref and decision.approval_ref.startswith("AUTO-JEV-")
    assert decision.action_type == "quarantine_and_revoke"
    assert decision.target_hosts == ["vm-a"]  # vm-b (NO_ACTION) excluded
    assert jev.last_state is not None
    assert jev.last_state["enrolled_auth0_hosts"] == ["vm-a"]

    runtime = VegaRuntimeState()
    for ev in events:
        runtime.record_event(ev)
    runtime.council_signal = signal
    enforced = await warden.enforce_decision(decision, runtime)
    assert enforced.execution_status == "contained_dry_run"
    assert runtime.threat_mode == "CONTAINED"
    assert next(n for n in runtime.nodes if n.source_id == "vm-a").status == "isolated"
    assert next(n for n in runtime.nodes if n.source_id == "vm-b").status == "healthy"


async def test_jev_low_confidence_fails_closed_to_human():
    signal, findings, events = _fixture()
    assessment = _assessment([_verdict("vm-a", "CONTAIN")], signal_id=signal.signal_id)
    jev = StubJev(
        JevEvaluation(
            available=True,
            action_choice="quarantine_host",
            confidence=0.52,
            probabilities={"quarantine_host": 0.64, "escalate_human": 0.36},
            credential_compromise=0.2,
            host_compromise=0.75,
            safe_to_automate=0.45,
            model="jev-1.13.0",
        )
    )
    warden = JevWardenService(jev=jev, executor=DryRunContainmentExecutor())

    decision = await warden.evaluate(assessment, signal=signal, findings=findings, events=events)
    assert decision is not None
    assert decision.requires_human_approval is True
    assert decision.approval_status == "pending"
    assert decision.execution_status == "awaiting_authorization"
    assert any(c.id == "jev-confidence" and not c.passed for c in decision.policy_checks)


async def test_jev_unavailable_fails_closed_to_human():
    signal, findings, events = _fixture()
    assessment = _assessment([_verdict("vm-a", "CONTAIN")], signal_id=signal.signal_id)
    evaluator = TypeSafeJevEvaluator(api_key="")
    warden = JevWardenService(jev=evaluator, executor=DryRunContainmentExecutor())

    decision = await warden.evaluate(assessment, signal=signal, findings=findings, events=events)
    assert decision is not None
    assert decision.requires_human_approval is True
    assert decision.execution_status == "awaiting_authorization"
    assert decision.jev_decision is not None
    assert decision.jev_decision["available"] is False

    signal, findings, events = _fixture()

    assert await warden.evaluate(assessment, signal=signal, findings=findings, events=events) is None

async def test_live_executor_runs_vault_auth0_and_iptables(monkeypatch):
    calls: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = []
    auth0_calls: list[tuple[str, bool]] = []

    executor = LiveContainmentExecutor(
        auth0_domain="example.us.auth0.com",
        auth0_client_id="warden-m2m",
        auth0_client_secret="REDACTED",
        vm_subjects={"vm-a": "auth0|6b01f488d9d84efdf43850d4"},
        telemetry_host="10.97.0.1",
    )

    async def fake_multipass(host: str, args: list[str], *, stdin_text: str | None = None):
        calls.append((host, args))
        return 0, "", ""

    async def fake_auth0(user_id: str, *, blocked: bool):
        auth0_calls.append((user_id, blocked))

    monkeypatch.setattr(executor, "_run_multipass", fake_multipass)
    monkeypatch.setattr(executor, "_set_auth0_blocked", fake_auth0)

    res = await executor.execute("quarantine_and_revoke", ["vm-a"])
    assert res.succeeded is True
    assert res.isolated_hosts == ["vm-a"]
    assert res.revoked_subjects == ["auth0|6b01f488d9d84efdf43850d4"]
    assert auth0_calls == [("auth0|6b01f488d9d84efdf43850d4", True)]
    assert len(calls) == 2  # 1 Vault blocked-users update + 1 iptables quarantine

    # Live mode sets execution_status="contained" (not contained_dry_run)
    warden = JevWardenService(
        jev=StubJev(
            JevEvaluation(
                available=True,
                action_choice="quarantine_and_revoke",
                confidence=0.95,
                probabilities={"quarantine_and_revoke": 0.96},
                credential_compromise=0.95,
                host_compromise=0.95,
                safe_to_automate=0.95,
                model="jev-1.13.0",
            )
        ),
        executor=executor,
        vm_subjects={"vm-a": "auth0|6b01f488d9d84efdf43850d4"},
    )
    signal, findings, events = _fixture()
    assessment = _assessment([_verdict("vm-a", "CONTAIN")], signal_id=signal.signal_id)
    decision = await warden.evaluate(assessment, signal=signal, findings=findings, events=events)
    assert decision is not None and decision.dry_run is False

    runtime = VegaRuntimeState()
    for ev in events:
        runtime.record_event(ev)
    runtime.council_signal = signal
    enforced = await warden.enforce_decision(decision, runtime)
    assert enforced.execution_status == "contained"
    assert runtime.threat_mode == "CONTAINED"

    # Release restores VM + Auth0
    await executor.release_all(["vm-a"])
    assert ("auth0|6b01f488d9d84efdf43850d4", False) in auth0_calls


async def test_oracle_bridge_invokes_warden_callback():
    signal, findings, events = _fixture()
    runtime = VegaRuntimeState()
    for ev in events:
        runtime.record_event(ev)
    runtime.council_signal = signal

    seen: list[str] = []

    async def on_assessment(assessment, sig, _findings, _events):
        seen.append(f"{assessment.signal_id}:{sig.severity}")

    bridge = OracleBridge(runtime, mock=True, on_assessment=on_assessment)
    assessment = await bridge.handle_signal(signal, findings)
    assert assessment is not None
    assert seen == [f"{signal.signal_id}:SEV1"]


async def test_typesafe_jev_evaluator_parses_system_one_response():
    import httpx2

    def handler(request: httpx2.Request) -> httpx2.Response:
        assert request.url.path == "/v1/systemone"
        return httpx2.Response(
            200,
            json={
                "model": "jev-1.13.0",
                "usage": {"input_tokens": 120, "output_tokens": 4},
                "answers": {
                    "containment_action": {
                        "type": "choice",
                        "choice": "revoke_credentials",
                        "confidence": 0.91,
                        "probabilities": {
                            "revoke_credentials": 0.93,
                            "quarantine_host": 0.05,
                            "quarantine_and_revoke": 0.02,
                            "escalate_human": 0.0,
                        },
                    },
                    "credential_compromise": {"type": "noul", "noul": 0.94},
                    "host_compromise": {"type": "noul", "noul": 0.22},
                    "safe_to_automate": {"type": "noul", "noul": 0.89},
                },
            },
        )

    from typesafe_sdk import AsyncTypeSafeClient, Choice, Noul

    transport = httpx2.MockTransport(handler)
    async with AsyncTypeSafeClient(api_key="REDACTED", transport=transport) as client:
        resp = await client.system_one(
            state={"host": "vm-a"},
            questions={
                "containment_action": Choice(
                    instructions="pick",
                    criteria={
                        "revoke_credentials": "revoke",
                        "quarantine_host": "quarantine",
                        "quarantine_and_revoke": "both",
                        "escalate_human": "human",
                    },
                ),
                "credential_compromise": Noul(instructions="cred"),
                "host_compromise": Noul(instructions="host"),
                "safe_to_automate": Noul(instructions="safe"),
            },
        )
    assert resp.choices["containment_action"].choice == "revoke_credentials"
    assert resp.choices["containment_action"].confidence == pytest.approx(0.91)
    assert resp.nouls["credential_compromise"].noul == pytest.approx(0.94)

Reference

# Models

Jev is TypeSafe’s flagship model and the first [System One model](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one). Every model on this page is served by the same endpoint, `POST /v1/systemone`. The request’s `model` field selects which one handles it; see the [API reference](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api) for the full request shape.

## Navigate to header: Current modelsCurrent models

|  | Jev 1.14 | Jev 1.13 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model ID | `jev-1.14.0` | `jev-1.13.0` |
| Price (per Btok / per Mtok) | $42 / $0.042 | $42 / $0.042 |
| Context length | 64k per-request / 32k per-question | 64k per-request / 32k per-question |
| Input | Text, images | Text, images |
| Question types | Choice, Score, Noul, Box | Choice, Score, Noul |

Jev 1.14 is the newest Jev release, available from October 14, 2026.

-   **Price:** You pay per input token. Output tokens are free. A Btok is a billion tokens and an Mtok is a million tokens.
-   **Context length:** Two limits, the per-request context and the per-question context. See Context length. To raise both, see Long context.
-   **Input:** Jev reads natural-language text, sent as a string, a JSON object, or an array of text values. It also reads PNG and JPEG [images](https://docs.typesafe.ai/images) anywhere in the request. It does not natively accept audio or video (yet). See [State](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state) for the shapes `state` accepts.
-   **Question types:** [Box](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/box) questions need Jev 1.14.

## Navigate to header: Context lengthContext length

Jev ingests the `state` once and evaluates every question against it in parallel. A request has to fit two context limits:

-   **Per-request context** (`per_request_context`): the `state` plus all questions combined.
-   **Per-question context** (`per_question_context`): the `state` plus any one question.

There is no separate limit on the number of questions in a request. Any number of questions is allowed as long as the request fits both limits. See [Speculative fan-out](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/fan-out) for packing many questions into one request, and [Model jaggedness](https://docs.typesafe.ai/model-jaggedness) for how accuracy shifts as the state grows. To raise both limits, see Long context.

### Navigate to header: Long contextLong context

Long context is off by default and works on both Jev 1.14 and Jev 1.13. To turn it on, send the `TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context: true` header with each request that needs it. With the header, the per-request context and the per-question context are both 262k tokens. Requests without the header keep the default limits in the table above.

```
curl https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TYPESAFE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context: true" \
  -d '{
    "model": "jev-latest",
    "state": "<a long contract, transcript, or record>",
    "questions": {
      "has_termination_clause": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Does the `state` include a clause that lets either party end the agreement early?"
      }
    }
  }'
```

Long context costs the same per token as any other request. It is slower and less accurate than staying within the default limits, so turn it on only for requests that need it.

## Navigate to header: Rate limitsRate limits

Rate limits are set per organization. Your organization’s current limits are in the [developer console](https://console.typesafe.ai/rate-limits). Limits are measured in tokens per second and requests per second. A request over either limit returns `429 Too Many Requests`. Our [client SDKs](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk) retry these requests by default, waiting longer between each attempt, and follow the `retry-after` header when the response includes one. If you call the HTTP API directly, see [Handling rate limits](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api/errors#handling-rate-limits). Higher limits are available on custom and enterprise plans. To request a higher limit, fill out the [rate limit increase request form](https://support.typesafe.ai/forms/rate-limit-increase-request).

## Navigate to header: AliasesAliases

An alias is a model name that points to a versioned model ID. Send it in the `model` field the same way you send a model ID.

| Alias | Points to | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `jev-latest` | `jev-1.14.0` | The most recent stable, official release. The default in our client SDKs, and the name the examples in these docs use. |
| `jev-preview` | `jev-1.14.0` | The most recent release, official or not. Moves ahead of `jev-latest` when a preview build is available. |

`jev-preview` currently points to the same model as `jev-latest`. There is no preview build available right now.

An alias moves when a new release ships, so its answers can change without any change to your code. Each response’s `model` field gives the versioned ID that answered, so you can log which model produced each result. If you have tuned confidence thresholds against one version, send that version’s ID instead of the alias, and switch to the new version when you are ready.

## Navigate to header: Customizing JevCustomizing Jev

Jev is not fine-tuned or LoRA-adapted with customer data. It is trained with [RLCD](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/machine-learning-primer) to return calibrated decisions, and the same weights serve every account. You shape its answers to your domain through the request rather than through per-account weights:

-   Put your proprietary content, records, and reference material in the `state` field. See [State](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state).
-   Encode your domain rules and boundary cases in the `instructions` and `criteria` of each question. See [How to build with TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one) and [Advanced: structure](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/advanced).
-   Decompose broad judgments into atomic questions and combine the outputs in code. See [Composite scoring](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/composite-scoring) and the [AutoResearch cookbook](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/autoresearch_feature_discovery) for training a downstream classical model on Jev’s probabilities.

## Navigate to header: Data handlingData handling

Jev is not trained on customer requests or responses. See [Legal](https://docs.typesafe.ai/legal) for the Data Processing Agreement, the Privacy Policy, and details on zero data retention (ZDR) for enterprise customers.

## Navigate to header: Listing modelsListing models

`GET /v1/models` returns the names your account can send in the `model` field, each with a description and a release date. It currently lists the aliases. Versioned IDs such as `jev-1.14.0` are accepted by the `model` field whether or not they appear in the list.

```
curl https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TYPESAFE_API_KEY"
```

## Findings

* **Official Direct Provider Pricing:** TypeSafe AI publishes direct model rates under its documentation and official model endpoints (`api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone`) for its System One decision models (`jev-1.13.0` and `jev-1.14.0`):
  * **Input Cost:** `$42` per billion tokens, or `$0.042` per million tokens (`$0.04` / 1M reported on specific routes).
  * **Output Cost:** Free ($0) because Jev does not generate conversational text or prose. 
  * **Exact Quote (Documentation):** `Price (per Btok / per Mtok), $42 / $0.042` and `"Price: You pay per input token. Output tokens are free. A Btok is a billion tokens and an Mtok is a million tokens."`

* **Gateways and Third-Party Interfaces:**
  * **OpenRouter / Opper / LLM Gateways:** These services host or pass through TypeSafe AI models (such as `jev-1.13` and `jev-1.14`). Gateways like Opper pass through the base provider rate without token markups while applying their own platform/gateway fees (e.g., 3% on credit purchases or control plane subscription tiers).
  * **Independent Developer Tools / Wrappers:** Third-party developer community tools (e.g., independent playgrounds and developer wrappers) reference prepaid balance structures starting from `$5` credits ("Prepaid packs from $5 — credits never expire"), but these are features of third-party tooling/gateways rather than an officially documented top-up tier directly hosted on `typesafe.ai`.

## Gaps

* **Direct Provider Top-Up Tiers:** Official documentation from TypeSafe AI specifies token input/output costs (`$0.042` per million input tokens) but does not explicitly detail an official direct-provider credit top-up schedule or a `$5` minimum tier on its native site (such tier descriptions appear primarily on independent third-party wrappers or community developer tool portals).

    async def _run_multipass(
        self,
        host: str,
        args: list[str],
        *,
        stdin_text: str | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
        if not _HOST_RE.fullmatch(host):
            raise ValueError(f"Refusing unsafe host identifier: {host!r}")
        proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
            "multipass",
            "exec",
            host,
            "--",
            *args,
            stdin=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE if stdin_text is not None else asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
        )
        try:
            stdout_b, stderr_b = await asyncio.wait_for(
                proc.communicate(stdin_text.encode() if stdin_text is not None else None),
                timeout=self.command_timeout,
            )
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            proc.kill()
            await proc.wait()
            raise TimeoutError(f"multipass exec timed out on {host}") from None
        return (

In `backend/vega/council/enforcer.py:249`, Warden adds a quarantine chain at the **top of the VM’s outbound firewall**. These are the two key rules:

```bash
iptables -A VEGA_QUARANTINE -j DROP
iptables -I OUTPUT 1 -j VEGA_QUARANTINE
```

The chain allows loopback and TCP traffic to the configured telemetry host on ports `8000` and `8001`. It drops DNS and everything else.

There’s **no exception for SSH replies**, so the rule can cut off the same `multipass exec` connection that installed it. That would explain why Multipass timed out even if the quarantine took effect.
what is this for?

It’s Warden’s **network quarantine**. If Warden decides a VM is compromised, the rule blocks it from sending data out or contacting an attacker, while still letting it send telemetry to VEGA so you can monitor it.

That’s separate from credential blocking, which stops the affected user from accessing Vault. The Multipass timeout is an unintended side effect: the quarantine can also block the connection Warden uses to manage the VM.

"""Real and dry-run containment executors for Warden (Auth0, Vault, Multipass VM iptables)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import logging
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Protocol
from urllib.parse import quote

import httpx

from ..models import WardenActionType, WardenAuditEntry

LOG = logging.getLogger("vega.warden.enforcer")

_HOST_RE = re.compile(r"^vm-[a-z0-9-]+$")
_AUTH0_SUB_RE = re.compile(r"^auth0\|[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$")
_AUTH0_DOMAIN_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9-]+(?:\.[a-z0-9-]+)*\.auth0\.com$")
_BLOCKED_USERS_PATH = "/etc/vega-auth0-vault/blocked-users"
_VAULT_UNIT_PATH = "/etc/systemd/system/vega-auth0-vault.service"


def _now_ts() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%H:%M:%S.%f")[:-3] + "Z"


def _audit(actor: str, message: str, status: str = "ok") -> WardenAuditEntry:
    return WardenAuditEntry(
        id=f"aud-{int(datetime.now(timezone.utc).timestamp() * 1000)}-{id(message) % 10000}",
        timestamp=_now_ts(),
        actor=actor,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        message=message,
        status=status,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    )


@dataclass
class ExecutionResult:
    succeeded: bool
    entries: list[WardenAuditEntry]
    isolated_hosts: list[str]
    revoked_subjects: list[str]
    """Executes real containment on Multipass VMs, local Vault, and Auth0 Management API."""

    dry_run: bool = False

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        auth0_domain: str,
        auth0_client_id: str,
        auth0_client_secret: str,
        vm_subjects: dict[str, str],
        telemetry_host: str = "10.97.0.1",
        command_timeout: float = 15.0,
    ) -> None:
        self.auth0_domain = auth0_domain.strip()
        self.auth0_client_id = auth0_client_id.strip()
        self.auth0_client_secret = REDACTED
        self.vm_subjects = dict(vm_subjects)
        self.telemetry_host = telemetry_host.strip()
        self.command_timeout = command_timeout
        self._revoked_subjects: set[str] = set()
        self._quarantined_hosts: set[str] = set()

    async def _run_multipass(
        self,
        host: str,
        args: list[str],
        *,
        stdin_text: str | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
        if not _HOST_RE.fullmatch(host):
            raise ValueError(f"Refusing unsafe host identifier: {host!r}")
        proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
            "multipass",
            "exec",
            host,
            "--",
            *args,
            stdin=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE if stdin_text is not None else asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
        )
        try:
            stdout_b, stderr_b = await asyncio.wait_for(
                proc.communicate(stdin_text.encode() if stdin_text is not None else None),
                timeout=self.command_timeout,
            )
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            proc.kill()
            await proc.wait()

        return (

"""Exercise the quarantine shell script with fake guest commands; never touch a VM."""

import os
import subprocess

import pytest

from vega.council.enforcer import LiveContainmentExecutor


@pytest.fixture
def quarantine_guest(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    executor = LiveContainmentExecutor(
        auth0_domain="", auth0_client_id="", auth0_client_secret="", vm_subjects={},
    )
    log = tmp_path / "firewall.log"
    log.touch()
    guest_env = {"PATH": f"{tmp_path}:{os.defpath}", "FIREWALL_LOG": str(log)}
    for name, stub in {
        "sudo": 'set -eu\n[[ "$1" == -n ]]\nshift\nunset SSH_CONNECTION\nexec "$@"',
        "iptables": 'printf "%s\\n" "$*" >> "$FIREWALL_LOG"\n[[ "$1" != -C ]]',
        "pkill": "exit 1",
    }.items():
        command = tmp_path / name
        command.write_text(f"#!/bin/bash\n{stub}\n")
        command.chmod(0o700)

    async def run_multipass(host, args, *, stdin_text=None):
        assert host == "vm-a"
        result = subprocess.run(
            args, input=stdin_text, text=True, capture_output=True, env=guest_env, timeout=5,
        )
        return result.returncode, result.stdout.strip(), result.stderr.strip()

    monkeypatch.setattr(executor, "_run_multipass", run_multipass)
    return executor, guest_env, log


async def test_quarantine_keeps_only_reply_traffic_for_multipass_ssh(quarantine_guest):
    executor, guest_env, log = quarantine_guest
    guest_env["SSH_CONNECTION"] = "192.0.2.10 50954 192.0.2.11 22"
    await executor._apply_vm_quarantine("vm-a")
    rules = log.read_text().splitlines()
    ssh_reply = (
        "-A VEGA_QUARANTINE -s 192.0.2.11/32 -d 192.0.2.10/32 -p tcp --sport 22 "
        "-m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED --ctdir REPLY -j ACCEPT"
    )
    assert [rule for rule in rules if "conntrack" in rule] == [ssh_reply]
    assert rules.index(ssh_reply) < rules.index("-A VEGA_QUARANTINE -j DROP")
    assert rules[-1] == "-I OUTPUT 1 -j VEGA_QUARANTINE"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("connection", [None, "999.0.0.1 50000 192.0.2.11 22", "192.0.2.10 50954 192.0.2.11 0"])
async def test_quarantine_leaves_rules_unchanged_without_valid_management_connection(quarantine_guest, connection):
    executor, guest_env, log = quarantine_guest
    if connection is not None:
        guest_env["SSH_CONNECTION"] = connection
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="quarantine unchanged"):
        await executor._apply_vm_quarantine("vm-a")
    assert log.read_text() == ""

"""Structured LLM reasoning abstraction for Sentinel scouts and Correlator."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio

from typing import Any, Protocol, TypeVar

from google import genai
from google.genai import types
